meta.title: Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cell-Derived Neural Progenitor Cells Produce Distinct Neural 3D In Vitro Models Depending on Alginate/Gellan Gum/Laminin Hydrogel Blend Properties.

extracted_by: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: Two alginate/gellan gum/laminin blends were used to print hiPSC-derived neural progenitors on an EnvisionTEC Bioplotter. The two blends, both within brain stiffness, produced distinctly different neural 3D models.

formulations.stiffness_note: elastic moduli within the range of brain stiffness
formulations.review_notes: Paper also uses a 1% ALG/0.01% LAM blend; which blend was printed vs cast should be checked.
formulations.name: 1.5% alginate / 0.5% gellan gum + laminin
formulations.key_outcome: Different ALG/GG/LAM blends steered hiPSC-NPCs into distinct neural 3D models.

evidence.quote: The 1.5% ALG/0.5% GG blend was prepared by mixing 3% (w/v) ALG stock solution to 1.5% (w/v) GG stock solution
The printing was carried out with an EnvisioTEC 3D‐Bioplotter (Manufacturers Series), using a nozzle with 200 µm inner diameter
The elastic moduli of the hydrogel blends lay within the range of brain stiffness.
